subject: Request: staged TTFT profile and progressive throughput exemption for streaming preview endpoints
messages:
From: Sara Li <sara@preview.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: sales@preview.ai
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: staged delivery TTFT and throughput profile for Preview streaming POC

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the POC looked great. We ran a short integration spike overnight and hit one sticky point around perceived latency for our users when using the streaming endpoint. Our UI progressively renders tokens in three phases (first chunk, progressive content, trailing completions). For the preview product we need an SLA carveout that recognizes a longer time-to-first-token (TTFT) for very large context loads (up to 180k tokens) but guarantees a progressive ramp to a sustained token/sec rate once the first chunk is delivered.

Key requests: 
- Allow a staged TTFT profile instead of a single fixed 1st-byte commitment for the preview tier (acceptable TTFT up to 1.5s on cold requests with huge KV loads).
- Commit to progressive throughput: 20 tokens/sec for the first 2s after first token, then ramp to 120 tokens/sec sustained for the rest of the stream for requests under 90k tokens.
- Fallback behavior: if node is under capacity, serve a sync endpoint equivalent (with clear headers) instead of failing.

I'm attaching a short proposal (preview_staged_ttft_proposal_v2.pdf) and a small trace bundle (trace_samples_20270414.txt) showing realistic client renders. Can we route this to your SLA/CS team for review? We have internal timelines tied to our beta in mid-May.

Appreciate it,

— Sara
Sara Li
Head of Integrations, Preview AI
https://preview.ai
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:46:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: staged delivery TTFT and throughput profile for Preview streaming POC

Karthik / Marissa — forwarding Preview's request. They want an SLA carveout for the streaming preview flow: essentially a staged TTFT/throughput profile and a clear fallback to sync when capacity is constrained. They've sent traces and a short proposal (attached).

Why this matters: Preview is a mid-size partner with a stepped rollout — if we can offer a reasonable carveout for preview tier (short-lifetime exception) it unlocks a larger Dedicated opportunity next quarter. We should check risk around our TTFT instrumentation (first-token definition across streaming variants) and whether the progressive throughput numbers are enforceable in the runtime.

Can you triage? Specific asks: 1) technical feasibility / required changes to token emission guarantees; 2) impact to latency SLOs and whether we can gate by model/context size; 3) docs language for the carveout if approved.

Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: staged delivery TTFT and throughput profile for Preview streaming POC

Lauren —

Quick technical read: feasible with caveats. The runtime already supports progressive emission and KV-prefetching but we don't currently expose a multi-band TTFT SLA. Implementation considerations: 
- Define measurement points: TTFT must be measured after model warmup + KV load window; we can tag requests with a "preview.staged_profile" header so the service counts them against a separate SLO.
- Token/sec guarantees are workload-dependent; we can offer a probabilistic guarantee (p95 ramp behavior) for specified request shapes. For example: for requests <= 90k tokens we can commit to the ramp numbers you asked for at p95 across dedicated pool nodes with the preview profile.
- Fallback: we can automatically route to sync-compatible model variant when capacity constrained, but we need to surface that in the response headers and in telemetry for chargeback.

I'll put together a short runbook for operational detection (traces we need, telemetry flags) and a proposed SLA blurb. If Marissa and Rohan sign off on the risk/commitment, we can propose a 6-week pilot carveout with limits (cap on concurrent preview.staged_profile requests, minimum instance sizing).

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Product Manager, Serving Runtime
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: staged delivery TTFT and throughput profile for Preview streaming POC

Thanks — reviewed the traces. A few points from CS/Legal: 
- Time window: we can approve a temporary carveout for preview (30–60 day pilot) but need a clear termination clause and visible metrics so we can revert if it impacts other customers.
- Measurement: must be explicit about which model variants and quantization levels are covered. No blanket commitments across all model families.
- Billing/credits: if we miss the progressive throughput ramp at p95, Preview gets a partial credit for the call (formula to be defined).

Operational constraints: require Preview to tag calls with a preview_tier header and to limit maximum concurrent preview streams to 40 during the pilot. Also ask Preview to provide a small synthetic trace harness for reproducible repros.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Li <sara@preview.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>, sales@preview.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: staged delivery TTFT and throughput profile for Preview streaming POC

Sara —

Appreciate the level of detail and the traces. We can run a limited 45-day pilot with the staged TTFT profile you proposed, subject to the following terms (summary):

1) Scoped models/variants: only applies to the listed model families in the attached proposal (we'll confirm a short whitelist).
2) Measurement & headers: requests must include preview.staged_profile and preview_tier headers so we can separate telemetry. TTFT will be measured from request arrival to first token emission inclusive of KV load.
3) Throughput ramp: Redwood will target the progressive ramp (20 t/s first 2s, then 120 t/s sustained) at p95 for requests <= 90k tokens on the dedicated preview pool.
4) Concurrency cap: Preview will limit concurrent preview streams to 40 during the pilot.
5) Fallback: if capacity constrained, calls will be routed to the sync-compatible variant and responses will include X-Redwood-Fallback: sync.
6) Credits: if the ramp misses p95 during the pilot, Preview receives a pro-rated credit; full credit formula and post-pilot review will be in the pilot runbook.

Next steps: Karthik will deliver the runbook and measurement spec by EOD next Tue, Marissa will prepare the pilot legal addendum, and Rohan will map out the dedicated pool sizing needed. If that timeline works, we will kick off staging the week of May 3 and start the pilot the week of May 10.

Let me know if you want a quick call to finalize details.

Best,

Lauren Bishop
Head of Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference
